summary: Dubai's tourism department says citizens of more than 80 countries can get a visa on arrival in Dubai. It lists 90 days within six months for passports such as the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan and South Korea, and 30 days for others; under the EU–UAE visa waiver agreement, citizens of EU countries such as Germany, France, Spain and Italy can stay without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Other travellers apply for a tourist visa through airlines, hotels or travel agents, as the UAE government portal describes.

conditionalWaivers.text: Citizens of India, Kenya, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, the Philippines and South Africa (ordinary passports), and their family members, can apply online to the federal ICP for a 14-day visa if they hold a valid visa or residence permit issued by the US, the EU or the UK, or a valid residence permit issued by Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, Singapore or New Zealand (Indians may also use a US green card). The visa must be used within 30 days of issue, allows 14 days from entry and can be extended once for the same period. Fees are AED 100 issuance plus AED 100 smart-services fee. Dubai’s GDRFA also offers Indian holders of a US green card or US visa, or a UK or EU residence visa, a 14-day visa that it lists as a visa on arrival.

source.name: ICP — Issuance of a 14-day visa for nationals of certain countries residing abroad (service card)

notes: Duty-free allowance per the UAE government portal (citing Dubai's Passenger Customs Guide): 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 500 g of tobacco; and alcoholic beverages up to 4 litres or 2 cartons of 24 beer cans (355 ml each). Duty and VAT are charged on anything above these limits.

The Government of Canada says some medications legal elsewhere, such as codeine and psychiatric medications, are controlled substances in the UAE and illegal to bring in, even in small quantities, without prior permission from the UAE Ministry of Health. The UK Foreign Office adds that some products containing CBD are illegal.
The UK Foreign Office says there is zero tolerance for drug offences: you can be arrested for carrying even residual amounts, and the authorities count drugs in the bloodstream as possession.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says ATMs are available across the emirates and credit cards are widely accepted at main hotels, shops and restaurants, but smaller businesses may only accept cash.

safety.text: The Government of Canada says the crime rate is low and violent crime is rare, though petty crime such as pickpocketing and theft from cars may occur. The UK government tells British nationals currently in the Middle East to be prepared for possible flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures and potential travel disruptions.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The UAE government describes a desert climate: warm and sunny in winter, hot and humid in summer, and generally cooler in the eastern mountains. The Government of Canada says humidity and heat may be most severe in the hot season from June to September, and that sandstorms and dust storms may occur any time, particularly during the summer months.

tips.text: Check your medications before flying: the Government of Canada says codeine and psychiatric medications are controlled in the UAE and need prior permission from the UAE Ministry of Health, and that bringing banned medication without approval can mean confiscation, heavy fines or jail. The UK Foreign Office says the Ministry publishes the list of controlled drugs and that approval is applied for online.

During Ramadan, the Government of Canada advises against eating, drinking or smoking in public between sunrise and sunset. It says that in Abu Dhabi and Dubai restaurants stay open and serve food as normal, and most government and public-sector bodies work reduced hours.

The Government of Canada says drinking alcohol is legal only in private homes and licensed venues, and being under the influence in public is an offence; the UK Foreign Office adds that drinking or possessing alcohol is illegal in the Emirate of Sharjah. Canada adds that the legal blood alcohol limit for driving is zero, that verbal insults and obscene gestures may be criminal acts, and that laws on online behaviour, including social media, are strict.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the UAE?
faq.answer: No. The UAE Embassy in Washington says US citizens are not required to apply for a visa before traveling: a visa is issued upon entry, allowing a maximum stay of 90 days, non-renewable, whether continuously or intermittently, within 180 days calculated from the date of first entry. It adds that a fine of AED 50 is imposed for each day over the 90 days.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in the UAE?
faq.answer: Under the EU–UAE short-stay visa waiver agreement, citizens of EU countries such as Germany, France, Spain and Italy may stay in the UAE without a visa for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. The agreement does not cover Ireland.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens get a UAE visa on arrival?
faq.answer: ICP issues a 14-day entry visa to Indian ordinary passport holders who hold a valid visa, residence permit or US Green Card issued by the US, the EU or the UK, or a valid residence permit issued by Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, Singapore or New Zealand (issuance fee AED 100 plus smart-services fee AED 100; extendable once for the same duration). The UAE Embassy in Washington says Indian citizens with US visas, green cards, or UK or EU residence permits can obtain this visa on arrival for AED 100. Other Indian passport holders need a tourist visa arranged before the trip.

faq.question: How much does a UAE tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: GDRFA Dubai lists AED 200 for a 30-day and AED 300 for a 60-day single-entry tourist visa, in addition to value added tax (5%), and says the total amount may vary. ICP lists, for visas issued through tourism establishments, an application fee of AED 100, an issuance fee of AED 100 per month for a single entry or AED 200 per month for multiple entry, and a smart-service fee of AED 100.

faq.question: Do I need a visa to transit through Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faq.answer: GDRFA Dubai issues a 48- or 96-hour transit visa that lets a foreign national transiting through the country's airports enter as a visitor. Applications go through approved airlines; GDRFA names Emirates Airlines, Flydubai, Dnata and airport hotels as channels, and lists the fee as AED 50 plus the intermediary's service fee. The UAE Embassy in Washington says to receive a copy of the visa before traveling.
